name: Operational Data Table
purpose: Compare identifiable records and act on an explicitly scoped result set without confusing missing data, permission or selection.
useWhen: Several records share meaningful comparable attributes.
Operators need stable identity, sorting or scoped row and bulk actions.
avoidWhen: A narrative, product discovery gallery or a single detail view is the main task.
Spreadsheet editing or spatial scheduling requires a dedicated grid or calendar contract.

states.presentation: Show record identity, labeled status and result count.
Retain headers and scope; label stale rows if retained.
Explain first use and offer an authorized create action.

states.meaning: Only some records or actions completed.
states.presentation: Separate successful, failed and unavailable records; avoid a false total.
states.announcement: Some records could not be updated

states.presentation: Keep filters and page intent with a persistent retry message.

states.meaning: Action is unavailable for this role.
states.presentation: Explain denied capability without exposing restricted values.

transitions.focus: Retain sort header; announce resulting order.
Keep pagination control; announce page and count.
Retain checkbox; announce selected count and scope.
Keep focus unless initiating row was removed; then next record or heading.
Keep query trigger; do not focus a decorative illustration.
Keep bulk summary available; link failed record IDs.
Retry failed IDs only; retain summary focus.

visual.hierarchy: Collection identity and current scope precede column headings; record identifier anchors each row before secondary metadata.
visual.alignment: Align text to reading direction and comparable numbers to the trailing edge; align headers with their cell values.
visual.spacing: Use the same horizontal inset for caption, toolbar and first content column; separate bulk actions from row controls.
visual.typography: Use body text for values, a restrained header weight and secondary text for metadata; tabular numerals support comparisons where available.
visual.emphasis: Reserve strongest emphasis for record identity and the current task action; selection uses an additional labeled marker.
visual.surfaces: Use subtle row separators for tracking across columns; avoid a separate elevated card around every cell.
visual.proportions: Give identity and long names flexible width; keep status and numeric columns readable; wrap important names or expose full text accessibly.
visual.discoverability: Anchor the frequent permitted action near record identity, reachable at horizontal origin on narrow screens; secondary values/actions may use named details/overflow with a permission reason. Native scrollbar auto is the comparison default; additional controls and cues must be verified before considering local concealment.
visual.states: Show missing as unknown or unavailable rather than zero; status includes words, freshness and units where relevant.
visual.brand: Reuse existing text, border, status and focus tokens; do not invent an industry palette.

keyboard.result: Visit links, selection and actions in document order; cells are read through table navigation.
keyboard.focus: Visible control focus; no custom arrow interception.

keyboard.when: Sort button, row checkbox or action.
keyboard.result: Activate the named control and announce changed sort or selection.
keyboard.focus: Retain control or nearest surviving row action.

keyboard.when: Only when a separately implemented and tested interactive grid is explicitly chosen.
keyboard.result: Use the complete APG grid focus model; this table pilot does not supply editable-cell behavior.
keyboard.focus: A grid manages one tab entry and cell focus; never add role=grid solely because rows contain buttons.

accessibility.naming: Give the region a task-specific heading and each control a persistent name.
accessibility.semantics: Prefer native table, caption and associated headers. Sort uses a button and aria-sort on its header. Checkboxes have record-specific names. A selectable table remains a table; an interactive grid is a separate composite-widget implementation requiring managed arrow-key focus.

checks.requirement: Every task and recovery action can be completed with keyboard input.
checks.passEvidence: Record the starting focus, complete the task and verify a visible logical destination.

responsive.condition: Column comparison is the primary task and readable columns exceed available width, including tablet or enlarged text.
responsive.restructure: Keep a semantic table in one named horizontal scroll region with native scrollbar visibility (auto); preserve row identity and place the frequent authorized action beside the identity or in a persistent, non-overlapping action area without horizontal travel. Do not convert comparison tasks to cards automatically.
preservedInformation: Record identity and full name access
Every comparable column and selected scope
Prioritized authorized action without horizontal travel
responsive.focusContinuity: Retain record IDs, query and sort; reveal focused cells/controls without obscuring them. Restore the same record action after details.

responsive.condition: Individual record lookup or editing matters more than simultaneous column comparison on a narrow screen.
responsive.restructure: Use a task-focused row summary with identity, critical status/value and authorized primary action; disclose labeled secondary fields on demand. A summary is not a forced card layout. Keep one active semantic representation and offer comparison when the task still requires it.
preservedInformation: All secondary values through a named details control
responsive.focusContinuity: Details return to the same record; do not duplicate tabbable controls or lose selection on layout changes.

responsive.condition: No records are displayed: initial empty, zero matches, loading or error.
responsive.restructure: Keep query, scope and recovery meaningful; do not create an empty horizontal scroll track from a minimum-width header. Hide or constrain the unused table region while preserving loading/status announcements and Clear or Retry.
responsive.focusContinuity: Keep focus on the initiating query/control, or move deliberately to an announced recovery destination.

density.useWhen: Mixed input methods, occasional use or unfamiliar terminology.
constraints: Keep controls independently reachable without overlapping hit areas.
Allow user text sizing and wrapping to determine minimum row or field height.

density.useWhen: Repeated scanning by experienced operators with a measured information need.
constraints: Reduce surrounding padding before reducing readable text size.
Preserve focus outline clearance, labels and distinct control targets.

motion.purpose: Explain a local state change without interrupting the current task.
motion.trigger: User initiated disclosure or result replacement.
motion.reduced: Replace content immediately; keep textual progress and completion feedback.
motion.interruption: Cancel obsolete transitions; never queue animation behind new input or block retry.

recovery.explanation: Retain failed query scope and distinguish stale rows.
Retry failed actions without repeating successes.
Return to the unchanged collection; authorization is owned by the application.

checks.requirement: Long labels, absent values and permission restrictions remain distinguishable.
checks.passEvidence: Inspect narrow and wide views with synthetic long labels and missing data.

checks.requirement: Failure preserves user intent and exposes an operable next step.
checks.passEvidence: Inject failure, retry and confirm identity, entered values and focus remain coherent.

checks.requirement: Failure when ordinary page content produces unintended horizontal overflow; a declared two-dimensional comparison region is evaluated separately.
checks.passEvidence: At 375, 768 and 1440 CSS px and enlarged text, measure document width and locate the offending node; repair its layout instead of globally clipping overflow.

checks.requirement: Review each genuinely overflowing region for a perceptible cue or reachable alternative control, plus keyboard and touch access.
checks.passEvidence: Record axis, task, accessible name, focus path and cue/control; test keyboard scrolling or equivalent navigation and swipe. Hidden scrollbar alone is neither pass nor failure.

checks.requirement: Review multiple scroll owners; unnecessary same-axis nesting can strand focus, wheel or touch input.
checks.passEvidence: Inventory page, collection, filter and dialog scroll owners; justify containment per task and exercise boundaries. Region count alone cannot determine a failure.

checks.requirement: Failure when a layout change loses the focused record/field, enters a hidden duplicate or changes keyboard task order incoherently.
checks.passEvidence: Resize with a field or row action focused; preserve identity, draft/query and logical order, then complete the task in both Tab directions.

checks.requirement: Failure when a declared essential row action cannot be reached without horizontal travel in a narrow viewport.
checks.passEvidence: At 375 CSS px and scrollLeft zero, locate and operate the frequent permitted action; verify a denied record exposes a reason and no unauthorized action. Repeat at 768 and 1440.

checks.requirement: Failure when critical identity/value is clipped without an operable full-content route.
checks.passEvidence: Use long names, text enlargement and missing values; demonstrate wrap or keyboard/touch-accessible detail. Title-only hover text does not suffice.

checks.requirement: Review the responsive strategy against the actual task; hidden priority columns and automatic card conversion can impair comparison.
checks.passEvidence: Declare which values/actions are essential; complete both single-record work and cross-record comparison, recording any extra disclosure cost.

anatomy.purpose: Associate stable record identity with values.
Describe count, freshness and missing values.
Expose contextual row and bulk outcomes.

guidance: Use links for navigation and keep sort controls keyboard operable.

variants.useWhen: Operators act on one or more authorized records.
guidance: Store selected record IDs rather than row positions.
Header selection affects this page by default; offer a separately confirmed all-matching scope with count and exclusions.
Changing filters clears selection or explicitly asks to retain a named cross-filter scope; never silently broaden it.
Recheck permissions and record revisions at execution; identify unauthorized and failed IDs in partial outcomes.

composition.focusOwner: Table retains local control focus; workspace coordinates removed rows and detail return.
